newsitem.title: USA: Marvel bondholders battle Perelman in court today.
newsitem.headline: Marvel bondholders battle Perelman in court today.

text.p: Irate bondolders of Marvel Entertainment Group Inc's parent companies, led by investor Carl Icahn, take their fight to court, today hoping to derail Ronald Perelman's plan for Marvel's emergence from Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.

In court papers made available to Reuters, holders of $894.1 million of the parents' debt, secured by 78.8 percent of Marvel shares, have asked bankruptcy judge Helen Balick to remove an automatic stay so that they can cash in their collateral shares, trading at about $2 each.
Bondholders allege Perelman's plan to reimburse them $40.2 million or $0.045 on the dollar in exchange for the shares collateralizing their debt, is "an inside deal" intended to "deceive the court."

Perelman's reorganization plan is based on a series of interdependent deals which begin with an infusion of $365 million, or $0.85 per Marvel share, from his wholly-owned Andrews Group Inc. The money would be earmarked to buy the Toy Biz Inc stock not already owned by Marvel.

When creditors late last year said the Toy Biz buyout should belong to Marvel, not Andrews, Perelman filed for bankruptcy, rejecting a leter from Icahn offering "to infuse $350 million into Marvel...to acquire Toy Biz (and) avoid the uncertainties and disruption of bankruptcy."

"(Perelman) waltzed into court on the Friday between Christmas and New Years, touting a prepackaged reorganization of Marvel...and enlisted this court's assistance in (his) unconscionable attempt to maintain control of Marvel at all costs," court papers allege.

Should his plan be confirmed at a scheduled March 7 court hearing, Perelman would control 80 percent of new Marvel stock while bondholders' collateral would be diluted from 78.8 percent to 17.2 percent.

Bondholders also want Judge Balick to dismiss the Marvel bankruptcy cases, claiming no plan has a chance of succeeding without their support. They assert in court papers that "Marvel and its subsidiaries can continue to reorganize and to operate under the protection of this court."

"Perelman took the secured bondholders' money out of Marvel to build his personal empire, not Marvel's fortune...Perelman's attempt to enlist this court's assistance in ramming through this deal...is a galling abuse of process," court papers allege.
Since it is Judge Balick's practice to rule from the bench when possible, there could be a decision today.
